formulas.formula: See the whole picture: what you own, what you owe, and where you're headed.
1. Balances: list every account you own (assets) and every debt you owe, with its type and category.
2. Type each balance on January 1 in Start of Year, then the balance at the end of each month.
3. Skipped a month for an account (like your home or car)? Leave it blank: the last balance carries forward.
4. Monthly Summary, Breakdown and Dashboard update on their own.
5. Goals: set a net worth target and date to see if you're on pace. History: add past year-end numbers.
Everything you own minus everything you owe. Type debts as positive balances.
Once a month is plenty. Pick a day (like the 1st) and stick with it.
Use a fair estimate and update it a few times a year. Being consistent matters more than being exact.
Goals use your average monthly change this year to project where you'll be.
Make a copy, type the new year, and use December's balances as the new Start of Year.
Tinted cells: these calculate for you.
Green: net worth went up, or a goal reached or on pace.
Red: net worth went down, a goal behind, or an entry to check.
Thank you for your purchase! Watch it grow.
=IF(TRIM('Balances'!C5&"")="","Your net worth at a glance.",'Balances'!C5&": net worth at a glance.")
One row per account. Assets and debts both as positive balances. Leave a month blank to carry the last balance forward.
Net worth at the start of the year and at the end of each month you've filled in.
Your latest balances: what you own, what you owe, and your biggest accounts.
Set a net worth target and a date. Your pace is your average monthly change so far this year.
Type your net worth at the end of past years (oldest first). The last row is this year, from Balances.
